title: 1988 AHSME Problem 24
statement: An isosceles trapezoid is circumscribed around a circle. The longer base of the trapezoid is \(16,\) and one of the base angles is \(\arcsin(0.8).\) Find the area of the trapezoid.

solutions.text:
Let the shorter base be \(b\) and each leg be \(\ell.\) Tangency gives \(16+b=2\ell.\) If the base angle is \(\alpha,\) then \(\sin\alpha=\frac{4}{5},\ \cos\alpha=\frac{3}{5},\) and \(16-b=2\ell\cos\alpha=(\frac{6}{5})\ell.\) Solving gives \(b=4,\ \ell=10,\) and height \(\ell\sin\alpha=8.\) The area is \(\frac12(16+4)(8)=80.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: For a circumscribed quadrilateral, the sums of opposite side lengths are equal
Use \(\sin\alpha=\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\cos\alpha=\frac{3}{5}\) to relate the leg, height, and difference of the bases
